input.title: Complete Effect Retry Interpreter
input.proposal:
## Plan Overview

Complete the Hevy client retry migration begun in PR #1104 by moving the entire retry execution lifecycle into one Effect v4 program per logical request. The work will land on `feat/effect-retry-interpreter`, stacked from commit `1073abb` at the head of #1104.

The migration must preserve the current Promise-facing public API and runtime behavior while eliminating shared schedule state, making default backoff and resource cleanup Effect-native, and correcting the caller-deadline retry-wait lifecycle defect approved during planning.

## Expected Functionality

### Milestone: Effect Retry Interpreter

1. **Characterize independent retry state and lifecycle behavior**
   - Add regression coverage proving sequential and concurrent operations on one client have independent retry budgets, schedule attempt indexes, cancellation, and observations.
   - Cover retry-wait finalization, cancellation/deadline races, and exact attempt/completion counts.

2. **Build Effect-native attempt and backoff primitives**
   - Represent attempt failures and retry transitions with internal typed errors/unions.
   - Bridge fetch, response consumption, and optional custom sleep through Effect v4 primitives.
   - Use `Effect.ensuring` for attempt listeners, retry-wait scopes, and execution-signal cleanup.
   - Use Effect `Clock`/`Effect.sleep` for default backoff so the actual client path is controllable with `TestClock`.

3. **Integrate the per-request retry interpreter**
   - Replace the imperative retry loop and nested runtime crossings with one recursive Effect program and one `Effect.runPromise` boundary.
   - Instantiate `Schedule.toStep(createRetrySchedule(...))` separately for every logical request.
   - Preserve retry limits, exponential backoff/jitter, `Retry-After`, absolute and per-attempt deadlines, the single fresh-budget read deadline retry, method safety, commit-state metadata, observations, diagnostics, and exhaustion behavior.
   - Correct the explicit caller-deadline path so it does not open/log an impossible retry or leak an unfinished retry-wait scope.
   - Verify Node and Cloudflare Worker compatibility and review affected README guidance for accuracy.

## Architecture

The Kubb client remains the Promise-based adapter boundary. Inside each request, a single Effect program owns the request lifecycle:

1. Acquire the combined caller/deadline execution signal.
2. Create a request-local retry schedule step.
3. Execute one typed attempt Effect.
4. Classify failure through the existing pure safety and endpoint policies.
5. Return terminal errors immediately, refresh the deadline for the one special read retry, or advance the schedule and execute an interruptible backoff Effect.
6. Recurse with updated retry state.
7. Finalize signals, listeners, and observation scopes on success, failure, defect, or interruption.
8. Convert the final Effect to the existing Promise contract exactly once.

The schedule owns timing and retry index only. Existing client policy remains authoritative for whether retrying is safe. Public `HevyHttpError` remains the externally observable error contract; internal Effect failures must never leak as Effect causes.

Package direction remains `hevy-client -> operations -> core -> adapters`. No Node built-ins enter runtime-neutral packages, and generated client files remain untouched.

## Environment Setup

- Worktree: `/root/hevy-mcp-effect-retry-interpreter`
- Branch: `feat/effect-retry-interpreter`
- Stack base: PR #1104 head, commit `1073abb`
- Use pinned tooling through mise: Node `24.19.0`, pnpm `12.0.0`
- Effect requirement: `4.0.0-rc.112`
- No new packages, accounts, credentials, or environment variables are expected.
- `HEVY_API_KEY` is not required for deterministic implementation or validation.

## Infrastructure

No long-running services or ports are required. Validation uses local Vitest, Nx, Wrangler/Workerd, package builds, and mocked HTTP fixtures.

Boundaries:
- Do not modify generated files under `packages/hevy-client/src/generated/`.
- Do not touch the original checkout’s untracked `.pi-subagents/` or `.worktrees/` content.
- Do not push or modify PR #1104; this work remains on the new stacked branch until explicitly requested.
- Keep real credentials out of files, commands, logs, fixtures, and output.

## Testing Strategy

Workers follow strict red-green-refactor TDD.

Worker-level validation:
- Focused `hevy-client` retry, schedule, deadline, cancellation, and observation tests.
- `mise exec -- pnpm run test:unit`.
- For runtime compatibility changes: `test:worker`, `test:worker-http`, and `worker:dry-run`.
- Package type checking and formatting/linting before handoff.

Milestone gate:
- `mise exec -- pnpm run check`
- `mise exec -- pnpm run check:types`
- `mise exec -- pnpm run build`
- `mise exec -- pnpm run test:pr`
- `mise exec -- pnpm run test:performance`
- `mise exec -- pnpm run check:changeset`

A release-triggering changeset must cover `@hevy-mcp/hevy-client` and all shipped transitive consumers required by repository topology.

## User Testing Strategy

The user-visible surface is the client’s Promise API and the MCP adapters that consume it. Validation is black-box through mocked client calls and Worker HTTP integration rather than browser interaction.

Test evidence will include:
- Promise results and `HevyHttpError` projections.
- Attempt counts and observation ordering.
- Cancellation/deadline behavior with no extra fetches.
- `TestClock` advancement proving default client backoff timing.
- Worker HTTP retry behavior and successful Workerd bundling.

Live Hevy testing is intentionally excluded because production calls cannot deterministically provoke retry statuses, hangs, or timing races. This is not a mock opt-out from a real integration path; deterministic failure injection is the only reliable validation method for the behavior being changed.

## Mission Readiness

Verified available and functional:
- mise, pinned Node and pnpm
- Effect v4 RC APIs: `tryPromise`, `callback`, `ensuring`, `sleep`, `Clock.currentTimeMillis`, `Schedule.toStep`, and `TestClock`
- TypeScript, Vitest, Nx, Wrangler/Workerd, oxfmt, oxlint, and Changesets
- Focused client tests: 56 passed
- Unit lane: 873 passed, 1 skipped
- Worker, Worker HTTP, Worker dry-run, and type-check lanes all passed without `HEVY_API_KEY`

Resource classification:
- 8 CPU cores, about 13 GiB available memory during readiness checks
- Current system load already exceeds core count, while Vitest/Nx/Workerd fan out internally
- Maximum concurrent validators: **1**

The implementation and validation path is executable with no unresolved blockers.

## Non-functional Requirements

- Preserve all public Promise signatures and current successful/error response shapes.
- Preserve runtime neutrality across Node and Cloudflare Worker.
- No cross-request mutable retry state.
- No leaked timers, listeners, signals, fibers, or observation scopes.
- Deterministic tests for concurrency and timing-sensitive behavior.
- Maintain exact safety rules for reads, idempotent writes, and non-idempotent writes.
- Keep diffs incremental, reviewable, and compatible with repository lint, formatting, changeset, and Conventional Commit requirements.

+
+Each logical Hevy request executes as one Effect v4 program with one
+request-local retry schedule and one outer `Effect.runPromise` boundary.
+Public Promise APIs and `HevyHttpError` behavior remain unchanged.
+
+## Components
+
+### Promise Adapter Boundary
+
+`createNativeClient` continues to satisfy the generated Kubb client's
+Promise-returning interface. It constructs the request Effect and runs it once.
+No Effect `Cause`, fiber, service, or internal tagged error may escape this
+boundary.
+
+### Request Interpreter
+
+The request interpreter owns the complete lifecycle:
+
+1. Initialize request state and acquire the combined caller/deadline signal.
+2. Create a request-local `Schedule.toStep(createRetrySchedule(...))`.
+3. Execute an attempt Effect.
+4. Classify the result with existing endpoint, execution-safety, and retry

+5. Finish attempt observations exactly once.
+6. Return terminal failures, refresh the signal for the one special read
+   deadline retry, or run an interruptible backoff Effect.
+7. Recur with updated immutable retry state.
+8. Finalize all active resources on every exit path.
+
+The interpreter may use Effect recursion or a generator loop internal to one
+Effect program. It must not call `Effect.runPromise` inside the program.
+

+
+The attempt Effect wraps fetch dispatch and response consumption. It tracks:
+
+- Request phase (`before-dispatch`, `dispatch`, `response-headers`,
+  `response-content`)
+- Whether a response was confirmed
+- Attempt deadline
+- Retry count
+- Observation scope
+
+Its typed error channel uses mission-internal failure types carrying the
+information needed by existing `HevyHttpError` projection. Public Effect error
+classes are not substituted where doing so would lose headers, cause,
+deadline, phase, or response metadata.
+
+### Transition Policy
+
+Existing pure functions remain authoritative:
+
+- HTTP method determines operation safety.
+- Phase and safety determine whether replay is safe.
+- Endpoint policy determines transient and expected outcomes.
+- Retry policy determines exponential delay, `Retry-After`, and jitter.
+- Existing metadata functions determine commit state and public diagnostics.
+
+The transition layer emits existing logs and observations. It distinguishes:
+
+- Terminal failure
+- Normal scheduled retry
+- Immediate fresh-budget retry after the first implicit read deadline
+
+A caller-supplied authoritative deadline must never open or log a retry that
+cannot execute.
+
+### Retry Schedule
+
+The Effect `Schedule` owns only retry indexing and delay calculation. A fresh
+step is created inside every logical request. Independent sequential and
+concurrent requests must never share schedule state.
+
+Normal backoff advances the schedule. The special fresh-budget read deadline
+retry does not sleep and should not consume normal scheduled backoff unless
+the finalized behavior-preservation tests require otherwise.
+
+### Clock and Sleep
+
+The default backoff path uses Effect `Clock` and `Effect.sleep`, making the
+actual client path controllable through `TestClock`.
+
+The public custom sleep hook remains Promise-based and is adapted with
+`Effect.tryPromise`. Its rejection must continue to become the existing
+classified backoff `HevyHttpError`. Both the operation signal and Effect
+interruption must prevent another attempt.
+
+### Resource Finalization
+
+Use `Effect.ensuring`, scoped acquisition, or equivalent Effect finalizers for:
+
+- Combined caller/deadline signal cleanup
+- Attempt-local abort listeners/controllers
+- Retry-wait scope completion
+- Any fiber or timer introduced by the migration
+
+Cleanup must run on success, typed failure, callback defect, cancellation,
+deadline expiry, and Effect interruption. Observer callbacks remain
+best-effort and must not cause duplicate request dispatch.
+

+
+1. The external API remains Promise-based.
+2. Public success and `HevyHttpError` shapes are behavior-compatible.
+3. There is exactly one Effect runtime boundary per logical request.
+4. Retry schedule state is request-local.
+5. Every attempt starts and completes observation exactly once.
+6. Every opened retry-wait scope finishes exactly once.
+7. Caller cancellation and deadline expiry start no later attempt.
+8. Reads and safe idempotent updates retain retry eligibility; non-idempotent
+   writes remain single-attempt.
+9. Explicit caller deadlines are authoritative and are never extended.
+10. Generated client files are not edited.
+11. `hevy-client`, `operations`, and `core` remain runtime-neutral.
+
+## Runtime Compatibility
+
+The implementation must work in Node 20+ consumers, the repository's pinned
+Node 24 development environment, and Cloudflare Workerd. No Node built-ins may
+be introduced into runtime-neutral packages.
+
+## Repository and Release Boundaries
+
+- Repository: `/root/hevy-mcp-effect-retry-interpreter`
+- Branch: `feat/effect-retry-interpreter`
+- Stack base: `1073abb` (PR #1104 head)
+- Effect: `4.0.0-rc.112`
+- Generated path `packages/hevy-client/src/generated/` is off-limits.
+- A non-empty Changeset must cover the client and all required transitive
+  shipped consumers.
+- Do not push or create a pull request unless the user explicitly requests it.
+
+## Validation Architecture
+
+Black-box validation uses mocked client requests and Worker HTTP integration.
+Live Hevy access is intentionally not used because retry statuses, hangs,
+cancellation races, and timing transitions cannot be reliably provoked against
+production.
+
+The actual default-backoff client path must be tested with Effect `TestClock`.
+Custom sleep compatibility remains covered through injected Promise hooks.
+Worker and bundle checks prove runtime neutrality.

2. **Explicit and implicit deadline retries currently open impossible retry lifecycle events.**  
   `canRetryAttempt` marks the first read deadline retryable without considering an explicit deadline (`hevy-client-kubb.ts:804-825`). `transitionAfterAttemptFailure` then emits completion and calls `createRetryTransition` (`:980-1029`), which advances the schedule, logs “Retrying,” and opens a retry-wait scope (`:939-975`). Only afterward does the loop reject an explicit deadline (`:1172-1181`). The wait scope is never finished. The implicit fresh-budget retry follows the same path, also violating the required zero log/wait behavior.

   **Required edits:** implement a distinct immediate-deadline transition before schedule/log/wait creation, and make explicit deadlines terminal before that transition.

3. **Observation scope failure can duplicate completion/finalization.**  
   `runRequestObservation` rethrows if `scope.run` invokes the operation and then throws (`:343-358`). The original operation continues asynchronously while the outer path classifies the scope error. It can later emit success after terminal failure, calling `finish`/`onRequestComplete` again (`:674-741`). The existing test at `hevy-client.test.ts:514-530` checks only one fetch, not late completion, finalizer cardinality, unhandled rejection, or settlement parity.

   **Required edit:** retain and return the already-started operation Promise when `run` throws/rejects after invocation; never classify the observer defect as the request failure.

4. **Attempt observation scope incorrectly wraps retry sleep.**  
   Retry sleep is passed through the failed attempt’s `run` scope (`hevy-client-kubb.ts:1197-1205`). The current assertion deliberately expects runs `[0,0,1]` (`hevy-client.test.ts:475-510`), but the architecture defines attempt-local scopes and separate retry-wait scopes. It should be `[0,1]`.

5. **Logger fallback can still alter execution.**  
   The logger callback is caught, but `console.error` is unguarded (`hevy-client-kubb.ts:302-310`). A failing diagnostic sink escapes. Existing coverage (`hevy-client.test.ts:140-164`) combines logger and completion failures and asserts little beyond rejection and sanitization.

Assert `instanceof HevyHttpError`, not merely absence of selected Effect fields. Clarify that curated methods expose decoded data, not internal `ResponseConfig`.

# Validation Contract

## Surface: Hevy Client Promise API

### Retry State and Policy

### VAL-RETRY-001: Sequential requests start with fresh schedule state
Two sequential GET operations through one client must each start at retry count zero, receive a complete independent retry budget, and use first-retry delay `[300,550)`; this remains true when the first operation exhausts its budget.
Tool: `mise exec -- pnpm exec vitest run packages/hevy-client/src/hevy-client.test.ts -t "sequential requests start with fresh schedule state"`
Evidence: Exit 0; per-request retry counts, delays, fetch counts, and settlements showing no state carried from the first request.

### VAL-RETRY-003: Concurrent requests have independent schedules
Two deliberately interleaved GET operations through one client must each start at retry count zero, receive their own configured budget and schedule indexes, and remain unaffected when the peer advances, exhausts, completes, or is cancelled.
Tool: `mise exec -- pnpm exec vitest run packages/hevy-client/src/hevy-client.test.ts -t "concurrent requests have independent schedules"`
Evidence: Exit 0; correlation-labeled attempts `[0,1]` or configured longer sequences, independent first-delay ranges, exact per-request fetch counts, and independent results.

### VAL-RETRY-005: Configured retry budgets are exact
For an always-transient GET and budgets zero through three, total attempts must equal `maxGetRetries + 1`, sleeps and retry-wait scopes must equal `maxGetRetries`, and the terminal error must report that exact retry count.
Tool: `mise exec -- pnpm exec vitest run packages/hevy-client/src/hevy-client.test.ts -t "configured retry budgets are exact"`
Evidence: Exit 0; table-driven attempt, sleep, wait-open, wait-finish, and `hevyRetryCount` values for budgets `[0,1,2,3]`.

### VAL-RETRY-029: Retry option normalization remains exact
`maxGetRetries` must honor zero, floor positive fractions, and use `MAX_GET_RETRIES` for `undefined`, negative, `NaN`, or either infinity; the normalized value, not the raw input, controls attempts, waits, retry indexes, exhaustion metadata, and the implicit operation-deadline budget.
Tool: `mise exec -- pnpm exec vitest run packages/hevy-client/src/hevy-client.test.ts -t "normalizes retry options"`
Evidence: Exit 0; table-driven raw and normalized values with exact fetch, wait, retry-count, maximum-attempt, and derived-deadline assertions.

### VAL-RETRY-030: Every attempt receives a fresh attempt budget
Each scheduled or immediate retry must receive a newly created, initially live attempt signal and a full per-attempt timeout capped only by the unchanged authoritative operation deadline; an aborted, expired, or settled prior-attempt signal must never be reused.
Tool: `mise exec -- pnpm exec vitest run packages/hevy-client/src/hevy-client.test.ts -t "each retry receives a fresh attempt budget"`
Evidence: Exit 0; distinct signal identities, live state at each dispatch, exact timeout boundaries under a controlled clock, and no later event delivered to a retired signal.

### VAL-RETRY-007: Success short-circuits the remaining budget
A GET that fails transiently once and then succeeds must make two attempts and one wait, return the second response, and perform no dispatch, wait, or observation for unused retries.
Tool: `mise exec -- pnpm exec vitest run packages/hevy-client/src/hevy-client.test.ts -t "success short-circuits the remaining budget"`
Evidence: Exit 0; successful payload, two fetches, one wait, and no events after settlement.

### VAL-RETRY-008: Retry indexes align across lifecycle events
For two transient failures followed by success, attempt starts and completions must carry retry counts `[0,1,2]`, waits `[1,2]`, and retry logs next-attempt values `[2,3]` of three, in lifecycle order with every opened scope finished once.
Tool: `mise exec -- pnpm exec vitest run packages/hevy-client/src/hevy-client.test.ts -t "retry counts align across observations and waits"`
Evidence: Exit 0; exact ordered event array, index metadata, and balanced attempt and wait scope counts.

### VAL-RETRY-009: Exponential backoff, cap, and jitter are preserved
Within one request, zero-jitter delays must progress `[300,600,1200,2400,4800,5000,5000]` milliseconds; with jitter, every delay must be at least its capped base and strictly less than base plus 250 milliseconds.
Tool: `mise exec -- pnpm exec vitest run packages/hevy-client/src/retry-schedule.test.ts packages/hevy-client/src/hevy-client.test.ts -t "exponential backoff"`
Evidence: Exit 0; exact zero-jitter sequence and boundary-random samples proving `base <= delay < base + 250`.

### VAL-RETRY-012: Default backoff uses the actual client TestClock path
The production request Effect used by the public client, without a custom sleep or test-only retry implementation, must be executed at its actual outer runtime seam with Effect `TestClock`: after a first 503 it remains pending, makes no second fetch one millisecond before the computed delay, and dispatches and resolves only when `TestClock` advances through the boundary, without wall-clock timer advancement.
Tool: `mise exec -- pnpm exec vitest run packages/hevy-client/src/hevy-client.test.ts -t "default backoff uses the Effect test clock"`
Evidence: Exit 0; identity/spy evidence that the production request Effect reaches the outer runtime seam, one fetch and pending Promise before the clock boundary, two fetches and resolved public value at the boundary, and no wall-clock timer or parallel test-schedule dependency.

### VAL-RETRY-013: Retry-After policy is preserved
For 429 responses, delta-seconds and clock-relative HTTP-date headers must set a lower bound, may exceed the 5000-millisecond exponential cap, and may never lower the current exponential base; malformed, negative, stale, or non-429 headers must fall back to normal exponential delay. Applicable delays retain bounded jitter.
Tool: `mise exec -- pnpm exec vitest run packages/hevy-client/src/hevy-client.test.ts -t "Retry-After policy"`
Evidence: Exit 0; deterministic cases for seconds, fixed-clock date, shorter and 20-second hints, malformed/negative/stale values, and non-429 status with asserted delay intervals and exact fetch counts.

### VAL-RETRY-018: Absolute deadline truncates an over-budget wait
A scheduled or `Retry-After` delay beyond the remaining absolute deadline must wait no longer than that budget, start no later fetch, and reject in phase `backoff` with `HEVY_DEADLINE_EXCEEDED`, outcome `deadline_exceeded`, and one balanced retry-wait scope.
Tool: `mise exec -- pnpm exec vitest run packages/hevy-client/src/hevy-client.test.ts -t "absolute deadline truncates an over-budget wait"`
Evidence: Exit 0; one fetch, controlled elapsed budget, public deadline fields, and exactly one wait open and finish.

### VAL-RETRY-019: Exhaustion preserves the terminal public error contract
After the final safe retryable failure, the rejected `HevyHttpError` must carry `HEVY_RETRY_EXHAUSTED`, `hevyRetryExhausted: true`, the performed retry count, false camel- and snake-case safety fields, outcome `terminal_failure`, and the final status, headers, phase, operation safety, and commit state.
Tool: `mise exec -- pnpm exec vitest run packages/hevy-client/src/hevy-client.test.ts -t "exhaustion preserves the terminal public error contract"`
Evidence: Exit 0; `instanceof HevyHttpError`, exact attempts and waits, and field-by-field error projection.

### VAL-RETRY-020: Reads retain endpoint and failure retry policy
`GET`, `HEAD`, and `OPTIONS` are reads; `PUT` and `DELETE` are idempotent writes; all other methods, including `POST` and `PATCH`, are non-idempotent writes. While budget remains, reads and idempotent writes may retry status `undefined`, 408, 429, and every 5xx status from 500 through 599 only when the code is undefined or is not `HEVY_REQUEST_ABORTED`, `HEVY_DEADLINE_EXCEEDED`, or `HEVY_RETRY_EXHAUSTED`. Statuses outside that set, those three codes, and every non-idempotent write are terminal. Every table cell must preserve its exact operation safety, phase-derived commit state, final safety, and attempt count.
Tool: `mise exec -- pnpm exec vitest run packages/hevy-client/src/hevy-client.test.ts -t "reads retry transient HTTP and network failures"`
Evidence: Exit 0; boundary-complete method/status/code table covering `undefined`, 408, 429, 500, 599, adjacent terminal statuses, all three excluded codes, and exact attempts, waits, outcomes, phase, commit, and safety metadata.

### VAL-RETRY-021: Idempotent PUT remains safely replayable
An idempotent PUT with a transient post-dispatch failure must expose `operationSafety: "idempotent-write"`, `commitState: "unknown"`, and `safeToRetry: true`, then wait once, replay once, and return the successful update.
Tool: `mise exec -- pnpm exec vitest run packages/hevy-client/src/hevy-client.test.ts -t "PUT retries remain safe with unknown commit state"`
Evidence: Exit 0; two PUT dispatches, one wait, retry metadata, and successful decoded result.

### VAL-RETRY-022: Non-idempotent POST remains single-attempt
POST must never retry a synchronous pre-dispatch failure, dispatch failure, transient HTTP response, response-content failure, or deadline expiry, regardless of read retry configuration; each terminal error must retain non-idempotent safety and phase/commit metadata.
Tool: `mise exec -- pnpm exec vitest run packages/hevy-client/src/hevy-client.test.ts -t "POST remains single-attempt for every failure phase"`
Evidence: Exit 0; one dispatch at most per table case, zero sleeps and waits, and exact public safety, phase, commit-state, and outcome fields.

When a first GET consumes its client-derived attempt timeout, exactly one second attempt must start immediately with retry count one, a fresh non-aborted signal and timeout budget, no sleep, no wait scope, and no advancement of normal backoff; it may resolve from that attempt. # Complete Effect Retry Interpreter

## Plan Overview

Complete the Hevy client retry migration begun in PR #1104 by moving the entire retry execution lifecycle into one Effect v4 program per logical request. The work will land on `feat/effect-retry-interpreter`, stacked from commit `1073abb` at the head of #1104.

The migration must preserve the current Promise-facing public API and runtime behavior while eliminating shared schedule state, making default backoff and resource cleanup Effect-native, and correcting the caller-deadline retry-wait lifecycle defect approved during planning.

## Expected Functionality

### Milestone: Effect Retry Interpreter

1. **Characterize independent retry state and lifecycle behavior**
   - Add regression coverage proving sequential and concurrent operations on one client have independent retry budgets, schedule attempt indexes, cancellation, and observations.
   - Cover retry-wait finalization, cancellation/deadline races, and exact attempt/completion counts.

2. **Build Effect-native attempt and backoff primitives**
   - Represent attempt failures and retry transitions with internal typed errors/unions.
   - Bridge fetch, response consumption, and optional custom sleep through Effect v4 primitives.
   - Use `Effect.ensuring` for attempt listeners, retry-wait scopes, and execution-signal cleanup.
   - Use Effect `Clock`/`Effect.sleep` for default backoff so the actual client path is controllable with `TestClock`.

3. **Integrate the per-request retry interpreter**
   - Replace the imperative retry loop and nested runtime crossings with one recursive Effect program and one `Effect.runPromise` boundary.
   - Instantiate `Schedule.toStep(createRetrySchedule(...))` separately for every logical request.
   - Preserve retry limits, exponential backoff/jitter, `Retry-After`, absolute and per-attempt deadlines, the single fresh-budget read deadline retry, method safety, commit-state metadata, observations, diagnostics, and exhaustion behavior.
   - Correct the explicit caller-deadline path so it does not open/log an impossible retry or leak an unfinished retry-wait scope.
   - Verify Node and Cloudflare Worker compatibility and review affected README guidance for accuracy.

## Architecture

The Kubb client remains the Promise-based adapter boundary. Inside each request, a single Effect program owns the request lifecycle:

1. Acquire the combined caller/deadline execution signal.
2. Create a request-local retry schedule step.
3. Execute one typed attempt Effect.
4. Classify failure through the existing pure safety and endpoint policies.
5. Return terminal errors immediately, refresh the deadline for the one special read retry, or advance the schedule and execute an interruptible backoff Effect.
6. Recurse with updated retry state.
7. Finalize signals, listeners, and observation scopes on success, failure, defect, or interruption.
8. Convert the final Effect to the existing Promise contract exactly once.

The schedule owns timing and retry index only. Existing client policy remains authoritative for whether retrying is safe. Public `HevyHttpError` remains the externally observable error contract; internal Effect failures must never leak as Effect causes.

Package direction remains `hevy-client -> operations -> core -> adapters`. No Node built-ins enter runtime-neutral packages, and generated client files remain untouched.

+# Mission Worker Guidance
+
+## Mission Boundaries (NEVER VIOLATE)
+
+**Repository:** `/root/hevy-mcp-effect-retry-interpreter`
+
+**Branch:** `feat/effect-retry-interpreter`, stacked from PR #1104 commit
+`1073abb`. Do not rebase onto main during the mission.
+
+**Ports and services:** No long-running service or claimed port is required.
+Do not start persistent watch, dev-server, or browser processes.
+
+**External services:** Deterministic mocked validation only. Do not call the
+live Hevy API and do not require, read, print, or persist `HEVY_API_KEY`.
+
+**Off-limits:**
+
+- `packages/hevy-client/src/generated/` must not be edited.
+- `/root/hevy-mcp` untracked `.pi-subagents/` and `.worktrees/` are user state.
+- PR #1104 and remote branches must not be modified or pushed.
+- Do not change public Node compatibility, package topology, or unrelated
+  adapters.
+
+If the feature cannot be completed inside these boundaries, return to the
+orchestrator.
+
+## Mission Directives
+
+**Tools:** Use mise for all Node/pnpm commands. Use named repository test lanes.
+Attempt the documented `entire graph` search first for locate/change work, but
+the CLI is known unavailable; after one failed probe, use focused repository
+search and reads rather than retrying.
+
+**Skills:** Invoke and follow `refactoring-playbook` for behavior-preserving
+migration and `codebase-design` when defining or changing the interpreter
+seam. Always follow `mission-worker-base` startup/cleanup.
+
+**Dependencies:** Use the existing `effect@4.0.0-rc.112`. Do not add or
+substitute an Effect version or retry library.
+
+**Other requirements:**
+
+- Strict red-green-refactor TDD.
+- Preserve Promise-facing APIs and `HevyHttpError` projections.
+- Keep exactly one outer Effect runtime boundary per logical request.
+- Create schedule state per request, never per client.
+- Default backoff uses Effect Clock/sleep; custom Promise sleep remains
+  compatible.
+- Preserve existing endpoint, safety, commit-state, retry, and diagnostics
+  policies instead of creating parallel policy logic.
+- No `any`, broad `unknown` helper contracts, manual casts, or Node built-ins in
+  runtime-neutral packages.
+- Observer callbacks are best-effort and may not duplicate dispatch or
+  completion.
+- Every opened attempt, signal, body, timer, fiber, and wait scope must finalize
+  exactly once.
+- Keep hooks enabled and use Conventional Commits with the Factory co-author.
+- Before each commit, add the required non-empty Changeset when the diff
+  triggers release coverage.
+
+## Coding and Architecture Conventions
+
+- Keep the Kubb client Promise signature unchanged.
+- Internal tagged failures must carry all metadata required for exact public
+  projection; do not replace `HevyHttpError` with a lossy Effect error class.
+- Prefer one deep request-interpreter module/seam over scattered Effect
+  wrappers.
+- Keep retry eligibility pure. The schedule owns retry index and delay only.
+- Use Effect finalizers rather than parallel manual cleanup paths.
+- A caller-supplied explicit deadline is authoritative and terminal.
+- The immediate implicit read deadline retry does not sleep, open a wait, or
+  consume scheduled backoff.
+

+
+Workers run the narrowest tests first, then:

+The milestone validator runs commands from `services.yaml` sequentially.
+Maximum concurrent validators is 1 due to current CPU saturation.
+
+Expected stderr from negative-path Worker tests is not a failure when the
+command exits zero. Live credential-gated lanes are out of scope.

+# Effect v4 Retry Patterns
+
+Worker-facing Effect v4 RC API constraints and approved patterns.
+
+---
+
+- Import `TestClock` from `effect/testing`.
+- `Effect.async` does not exist in this version; the callback primitive is
+  `Effect.callback`.
+- `Effect.tryPromise` accepts an interruption signal and must use an explicit
+  catch mapping.
+- Use `Schedule.toStep` for the interpreter because it must inspect/cap delay,
+  control wait observations, support custom sleep, and classify sleep failure.
+- `Schedule.toStepWithSleep` is unsuitable for this lifecycle because it hides
+  the sleep seam.
+- Schedule steps are stateful. Construct one inside every logical request.
+- Schedule completion uses `Pull`/`Cause.Done`; avoid stepping beyond the known
+  retry budget or handle completion explicitly.
+- Use `Clock.currentTimeMillis` and `Effect.sleep` for default backoff.
+- Use `Effect.ensuring` or scoped finalization for cleanup on success, typed
+  failure, defect, and interruption.
+- Do not pass the caller AbortSignal directly to `Effect.runPromise` unless
+  Cause-level interruption is projected back to the established public
+  `HevyHttpError`.
+- Build one request Effect and call `Effect.runPromise` once at the Promise
+  adapter boundary. Do not nest runtime executions.

+   - custom Promise sleep adaptation;
+   - exactly-once resource finalizers;
+   - one outer runtime boundary.

Worker-facing Effect v4 RC API constraints and approved patterns.

---

- Import `TestClock` from `effect/testing`.
- `Effect.async` does not exist in this version; the callback primitive is
  `Effect.callback`.
- `Effect.tryPromise` accepts an interruption signal and must use an explicit
  catch mapping.
- Use `Schedule.toStep` for the interpreter because it must inspect/cap delay,
  control wait observations, support custom sleep, and classify sleep failure.
- `Schedule.toStepWithSleep` is unsuitable for this lifecycle because it hides
  the sleep seam.
- Schedule steps are stateful. Construct one inside every logical request.
- Schedule completion uses `Pull`/`Cause.Done`; avoid stepping beyond the known
  retry budget or handle completion explicitly.
- Use `Clock.currentTimeMillis` and `Effect.sleep` for default backoff.
- Use `Effect.ensuring` or scoped finalization for cleanup on success, typed
  failure, defect, and interruption.
- Do not pass the caller AbortSignal directly to `Effect.runPromise` unless
  Cause-level interruption is projected back to the established public
  `HevyHttpError`.

## Hevy CLI Prefer the terminal? The separate [`@chrisdoc/hevy-cli`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@chrisdoc/hevy-cli) package reads workouts, routines, exercises, and body measurements directly from the Hevy API, and can create or update those resources with explicit confirmation. Deletion is not supported. ```sh npm install -g @chrisdoc/hevy-cli export HEVY_API_KEY=your-hevy-api-key hevy workouts list --page-size 10 hevy summary --weeks 4 ``` Add `--json` to any command for scripts and pipelines. The CLI is a standalone Hevy API client, not an MCP wrapper. See [`packages/cli/README.md`](packages/cli/README.md) for the full command reference, pagination behavior, and exit codes. `hevy-mcp` is an open-source [Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) server for the [Hevy](https://www.hevyapp.com/) fitness and workout tracking app. It lets AI assistants read, analyze, create, and update your Hevy workouts, routines, exercise templates, and body measurements through authenticated Hevy API requests. The repository is organized as a private workspace with explicit runtime boundaries: `@hevy-mcp/hevy-client` owns the web-safe Hevy client, `@hevy-mcp/core` owns MCP tools and server construction, `hevy-mcp` is the published Node.js stdio adapter, and `@hevy-mcp/worker` is the private Cloudflare HTTP/OAuth adapter. Only the Node workspace is publishable. > A Hevy API key, available with **Hevy PRO**, is required. ## See it in action [![Hevy MCP demo showing an AI assistant analyzing six weeks of Hevy training data](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/main/docs/assets/hevy-mcp-demo.gif)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/main/docs/assets/hevy-mcp-demo.mp4)

Click the preview to play the full-quality 18-second demo.

In the demo, the assistant retrieves real Hevy data and answers a multi-part training question with evidence from the user's workout history. ## What can you do with it? - **Analyze training progress:** summarize 1-12 weeks of workouts and body measurements in one tool call. - **Ask questions in plain language:** find recent sessions, frequently trained exercises, consistency gaps, routine details, or exercise history. - **Plan and log training:** create or update workouts, routines, routine folders, custom exercises, and body measurements. - **Search without huge responses:** discover routines and exercise templates with compact, AI-friendly results. - **Connect from your preferred MCP client:** use the hosted Streamable HTTP endpoint or run locally with Codex, Claude Desktop, Cursor, and other clients. - **Start without installing anything:** connect directly to the production Cloudflare Worker—no Node.js, package download, or Docker container required. - **Keep local control when you want it:** run the same server with `npx`, `bunx`, or the official Docker image. Try asking: > Analyze my training over the last six weeks. Show workouts per week, my most > frequently trained exercises, any obvious gaps or inconsistencies, and cite the > workout evidence you used. > Find my push-day routine and show its exercises and sets. > Compare my recent body measurements with my training consistency. > Create a completed workout from my saved routine. Ask me for any missing set > results before writing it to Hevy. ## Claude integration The repository includes a Claude plugin that connects to the hosted OAuth-enabled MCP endpoint without embedding a user's Hevy API key. ### Claude.ai and Claude Desktop In Claude, open **Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector** and enter: ```text https://mcp.hevy-mcp.dev/mcp ``` Complete the OAuth flow and enter the Hevy API key when prompted. The same remote endpoint can be used by Claude Desktop and other clients that support remote MCP connectors. ### Claude Code and Cowork The Claude plugin is defined by [`.claude-plugin/plugin.json`](./.claude-plugin/plugin.json) and [`.mcp.json`](./.mcp.json). Install it from this public repository or from the Claude Plugin Directory after publication. It adds the hosted Hevy MCP connector and the [Hevy workout skill](./skills/hevy-workouts/SKILL.md). See the [privacy policy](./docs/privacy-policy.md) for the hosted service's data handling details. ## Quick start ### 1. Get your Hevy API key Create an API key in [Hevy's API settings](https://www.hevyapp.com/api), then keep it somewhere secure. API access currently requires a Hevy PRO subscription. ### 2. Connect `hevy-mcp` to your client The hosted Cloudflare endpoint is the fastest way to start. It runs remotely, so your client does not need Node.js, Bun, Docker, or a local server process. #### Connect to the hosted endpoint Production URL: ```text https://mcp.hevy-mcp.dev/mcp ``` The endpoint uses Streamable HTTP. Send your Hevy API key as a bearer token on every request. ##### Codex Codex CLI, the Codex desktop app, and the IDE extension share the same MCP configuration. Make your Hevy API key available in the environment that starts Codex, then add the hosted server: ```bash export HEVY_API_KEY=your-hevy-api-key codex mcp add hevy \ --url https://mcp.hevy-mcp.dev/mcp \ --bearer-token-env-var HEVY_API_KEY ``` Codex stores the environment variable name, not the key itself, in its MCP configuration. Restart Codex or begin a new session, then run `codex mcp list` to verify the server is configured. ##### Other Streamable HTTP clients Clients that accept a remote MCP URL and fixed headers commonly use this shape: ```json { "mcpServers": { "hevy": { "url": "https://mcp.hevy-mcp.dev/mcp", "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer your-hevy-api-key" } } } } ``` Exact configuration keys vary by client. The hosted server requires support for Streamable HTTP and a fixed `Authorization` header. > [!IMPORTANT] > Treat the bearer value like a password. The Worker validates it with Hevy for > each request, does not store it, and forwards it to Hevy only as the required > `api-key` header. #### Run locally instead Choose local stdio if you prefer to run the server on your own machine or your client cannot attach a fixed authorization header to remote MCP requests. ##### Codex ```bash codex mcp add hevy \ --env HEVY_API_KEY=your-hevy-api-key \ -- npx -y hevy-mcp ``` ##### Claude Desktop or Cursor Add this `mcpServers` entry to your client configuration: ```json { "mcpServers": { "hevy": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "hevy-mcp"], "env": { "HEVY_API_KEY": "your-hevy-api-key" } } } } ``` ##### Google Antigravity There are two ways to configure the Hevy MCP server for Google Antigravity (`agy`): ###### Option A: Automatic Plugin Installation (Recommended) This utilizes the built-in plugin system: 1. Install the plugin: ```bash agy plugin install https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp ``` 2. Provide the `HEVY_API_KEY` in your host shell environment so the CLI child process can inherit it: - **Persistent:** Save the environment variable `HEVY_API_KEY` in your system/shell configurations: - **macOS / Linux:** Add it to your shell profile configurations (e.g., `~/.zshrc` or `~/.bashrc`): ```bash export HEVY_API_KEY="your-actual-api-key" ``` - **Windows:** Add it to your User or System Environment Variables. In PowerShell, you can run: ```powershell [Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable("HEVY_API_KEY", "your-actual-api-key", "User") ``` - **Temporary (Session-only):** If you do not want to persist the key, export it in your active terminal session before running `agy`: ```bash export HEVY_API_KEY="your-actual-api-key" ``` ###### Option B: Manual Configuration (No Plugin) If you prefer configuring it statically via the global configuration file: 1. Open your global MCP configuration file: - **Location:** `~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json` 2. Add the `hevy` configuration block under the `mcpServers` key. Make sure to merge this entry with any existing servers you have configured rather than replacing the entire file contents: ```json { "mcpServers": { "hevy": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "hevy-mcp"], "env": { "HEVY_API_KEY": "your-actual-api-key" } } } } ``` Common local configuration locations: - **Claude Desktop on macOS:** `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json` - **Claude Desktop on Windows:** `%APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json` - **Cursor:** `~/.cursor/mcp.json` Restart or reconnect the client after saving the file. ##### Any stdio MCP client Configure your client to launch this command with `HEVY_API_KEY` in the child process environment: ```bash npx -y hevy-mcp ``` `npx` requires Node.js 20 or newer. Restart or reconnect your client after saving its configuration.
Use bunx instead Requires [Bun](https://bun.sh/): ```json { "mcpServers": { "hevy": { "command": "bunx", "args": ["hevy-mcp@latest"], "env": { "HEVY_API_KEY": "your-hevy-api-key" } } } } ```
Use Docker instead Official images support `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`. Keep stdin open with `-i` because the container runs the stdio MCP server: ```bash export HEVY_API_KEY=your-hevy-api-key docker run -i --rm -e HEVY_API_KEY ghcr.io/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp:latest ``` For an MCP client, store the key in a protected environment file and configure the client to launch Docker: ```json { "mcpServers": { "hevy": { "command": "docker", "args": [ "run", "-i", "--rm", "--env-file", "/absolute/path/to/hevy-mcp.env", "ghcr.io/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp:latest" ] } } } ``` Pin an exact image tag such as `ghcr.io/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp:X.Y.Z` when you need reproducible upgrades.
You can also add the npm server to supported clients with [`add-mcp`](https://github.com/neon-solutions/add-mcp): ```bash npx add-mcp hevy-mcp --env "HEVY_API_KEY=your-hevy-api-key" ``` ### 3. Ask your first question Try one of these after restarting or reconnecting your MCP client: - “Give me a training summary for the last four weeks.” - “What routines do I have saved on Hevy?” - “Show my three most recent workouts.” - “Find exercise templates containing squat.” - “Which Hevy account is connected?” Your assistant should ask for approval before mutation tools when the client supports tool confirmations. ## How it works ```text Hosted: Your AI assistant → Streamable HTTP → Cloudflare Worker → Hevy API Local: Your AI assistant → MCP over stdio → local hevy-mcp → Hevy API ``` The hosted endpoint creates a fresh MCP server and Hevy client for each request. It validates the supplied key with Hevy, keeps no shared user session, and does not persist the key. The local server follows the same tool contract but runs on your machine and receives the key through its child-process environment. In either mode, read tools retrieve data; mutation tools create or replace data only when your assistant calls them. ## Guided prompts These server-provided MCP prompts coordinate common multi-step workflows: | Prompt | Arguments | Workflow | | ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `analyze-workout-progress` | Optional `weeks` from 1-12; default `4` | Calls `get-training-summary`, then analyzes workout activity and body-measurement trends from the returned evidence. | | `create-workout-from-routine` | Required `routine_id` and UTC `start_time` | Loads a routine, collects actual completed-set data and an end time, then creates a workout without inventing results. | > [!NOTE] > With MCP SDK v1.29.0, clients invoking `analyze-workout-progress` with its > default value must send `arguments: {}`. Omitting the entire `arguments` > object is rejected by that SDK version before the default is applied. ## Tools `hevy-mcp` registers 22 tools. Read-only tools are safe for exploration; create and update tools are exposed with MCP mutation annotations so compatible clients can request confirmation. | Category | Tool | Description | | ----------------- | ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Training analysis | `get-training-summary` | Summarize 1-12 weeks of workout activity and body-measurement trends in one call. | | Workouts | `get-workouts` | List workouts in Hevy API order, not by start time, with exercise and timing details. | | Workouts | `get-workout` | Get complete details for one workout by ID. | | Workouts | `get-workout-events` | List workout update and delete events since a timestamp. | | Workouts | `create-workout` | Create a completed workout in Hevy. | | Workouts | `update-workout` | Patch workout metadata by ID; `is_private` is required, while other omitted fields and all exercises remain unchanged. | | Workouts | `replace-workout-exercises` | Replace all exercises and sets; `is_private` is required and updated, while other workout metadata remains unchanged. | | Routines | `search-routines` | Search routine titles and return compact metadata for discovery. | | Routines | `get-routines` | List custom and default workout routines. | | Routines | `get-routine` | Get one routine and its exercise configuration by ID. | | Routines | `create-routine` | Create a reusable workout routine. | | Routines | `update-routine` | Replace an existing routine's content. | | Routine folders | `get-routine-folder` | Get one routine folder's metadata by ID. | | Routine folders | `create-routine-folder` | Create a routine folder. | | Exercise templates | `get-exercise-template` | Get complete metadata for one exercise template by ID. | | Exercise templates | `search-exercise-templates` | Search the full exercise catalog by title substring. | | Exercise templates | `create-exercise-template` | Create a custom exercise template. | | Exercise history | `get-exercise-history` | Get past performed sets for one exercise template. | | Body measurements | `get-body-measurements` | List dated body measurements. | | Body measurements | `get-body-measurement` | Get the body measurement entry for one date. | | Body measurements | `create-body-measurement` | Create a dated body measurement. | | Body measurements | `update-body-measurement` | Update the body measurement for an existing date. | `create-routine` and `update-routine` require a top-level `routine` envelope with a non-empty `exercises` array; each exercise must contain at least one set, and fields use snake_case at every level: ```json { "routine": { "title": "Full Body A", "folder_id": 123, "notes": "First four exercises are the minimum viable workout", "exercises": [ { "exercise_template_id": "30E293E3", "superset_id": null, "rest_seconds": 120, "notes": "Controlled active ROM", "sets": [ { "type": "normal", "rep_range": { "start": 6, "end": 10 } } ] } ] } } ``` The Hevy API currently exposes no delete endpoints for workouts, routines, routine folders, exercise templates, or body measurements, so there are no corresponding delete tools. ### Resources | Name | URI | Description | | -------------------- | --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | | `user-profile` | `hevy://user` | Authenticated Hevy user profile. | | `workout-count` | `hevy://workout-count` | Total number of workouts in the account. | | `exercise-templates` | `hevy://exercise-templates` | Full formatted exercise template catalog. | | `routine-folders` | `hevy://routine-folders` | Full formatted list of Hevy routine folders. | ## Hosted Cloudflare endpoint The production MCP server is live at: ```text https://mcp.hevy-mcp.dev/mcp ``` It is the quickest way to use `hevy-mcp`: there is nothing to install or keep running locally, and it exposes the same 22 tools as the npm package and Docker image. Clients must send their Hevy API key as a fixed authorization header: ```json { "mcpServers": { "hevy": { "url": "https://mcp.hevy-mcp.dev/mcp", "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer your-hevy-api-key" } } } } ``` The bearer value is your Hevy API key, not an OAuth token. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md#cloudflare-worker-development) for setup and for the distinction between self-hosting and the maintainer-only named environments. A Docker deployment must publish the port explicitly: ```bash docker run --rm -p 3000:3000 -e HEVY_API_KEY -e HEVY_MCP_HTTP_BEARER_TOKEN \\ ghcr.io/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp:latest --transport http --host 0.0.0.0 --port 3000 ``` This Node HTTP mode is distinct from the stateless Cloudflare Worker HTTP endpoint described above: the Node server owns stateful client sessions, while the Worker is designed for hosted deployment and does not import Node code. ### Cache behavior `search-exercise-templates` and `hevy://exercise-templates` share a server-scoped in-memory catalog cache: - Entries live for five minutes, and the cache holds at most one catalog. - Concurrent catalog requests share an in-flight fetch when possible. - `search-exercise-templates` accepts `refresh: true` to invalidate the cache. - Each hosted Worker request gets a fresh cache, preventing cross-key sharing. ### Local Node telemetry and privacy The local Node package enables project telemetry by default. It is local Node behavior only; the Cloudflare Worker does not import Node telemetry. Set `HEVY_MCP_TELEMETRY=0` before startup or import to disable all project telemetry. Only the literal value `0` opts out: an unset value, an empty value, `1`, `false`, and every other value remain enabled. The master setting takes precedence over `SENTRY_DSN` and packaged or runtime `OTEL_COLLECTOR_TOKEN` credentials, so the disabled path creates no telemetry exporters or periodic metric readers and makes no telemetry network requests. `SENTRY_DSN` remains a Sentry-only setting; when telemetry is enabled, an empty value disables only Sentry export. When enabled, actionable errors are sent to the Sentry project configured by `SENTRY_DSN`; Sentry performance tracing is disabled. Exception messages and stacks are bounded and scrubbed before export. Set `HEVY_MCP_TELEMETRY_DIAGNOSTICS=0` to keep structural traces and metrics while suppressing those details. Traces and metrics continue to be sent to the collector at and , which forward to Honeycomb. Metrics export every 30 seconds. The API key is never exported and is not used to derive a user identity. A per-failure diagnostic ID and OTel trace ID may be attached to actionable errors for support correlation. Structured telemetry contains only bounded service, release, transport, tool, outcome, error, count, retry, duration, session, cache, workflow, API method, normalized endpoint, and status fields. Exception messages and stacks are treated as diagnostic details: they are length-limited, scrubbed for credentials, URLs, and local home paths, and removed entirely when `HEVY_MCP_TELEMETRY_DIAGNOSTICS=0`. Prompts, tool arguments, tool results, request bodies, API keys, raw identifiers/queries, exact dates, workout/routine/folder/template/body-measurement content, names/titles/descriptions/notes, measurement values, arbitrary client metadata, and unnormalized endpoint paths remain prohibited. ## Security and mutations - Keep `HEVY_API_KEY` out of source control, URLs, logs, and screenshots. - Local clients provide the key through the child process environment. - Hosted clients send the key only in the `Authorization: Bearer` header. The Worker validates each key with Hevy, does not store it, and sends it upstream only as Hevy's `api-key` header. - Browser requests must come from an exact allowlisted origin. The default allowlist includes Claude.ai, ChatGPT, VS Code for the Web, and github.dev; self-hosted deployments can override it with `MCP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`. - Local development can copy `.dev.vars.example` to `.dev.vars` to disable Origin validation for MCP Inspector. PR preview Workers use the same development-only setting because their browser origins are dynamic. Never set `MCP_DISABLE_ORIGIN_CHECK=true` on a production Worker. - Create operations can produce duplicates when retried. Update operations replace existing records. Review tool inputs and use client confirmations. ## Troubleshooting - **The server does not appear:** restart or reconnect your MCP client after changing its configuration. - **`npx` fails:** confirm that Node.js 20 or newer is installed, then run `npx -y hevy-mcp --version` in a terminal. - **Codex cannot see the server:** run `codex mcp list`, then start a new Codex session after confirming the `hevy` entry exists. - **Hevy API returns 401:** the key is invalid, expired, revoked, or misconfigured. Verify or create an active key at [Hevy's API settings](https://www.hevyapp.com/api), then restart the client. - **Hosted authentication fails:** confirm the key belongs to a Hevy PRO account and is sent as `Authorization: Bearer `. - **Local authentication fails:** confirm the key is active and available to the MCP child process as `HEVY_API_KEY`. - **Need diagnostics:** set `HEVY_MCP_DEBUG=1`. Diagnostic output goes to stderr and does not interfere with MCP messages on stdout. If you find a bug or have a feature request, [open an issue](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/issues). ## Contributing Contributions are welcome. Developer setup, testing lanes, generated-client workflows, Cloudflare Worker deployment, and pull request rules are documented in [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md). ## License and acknowledgements - **License:** [MIT](./LICENSE) - **Credits:** [Model Context Protocol](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol) and [Hevy Fitness](https://www.hevyapp.com/)

# Effect Client Worker

NOTE: Startup and cleanup are handled by `mission-worker-base`. This skill
defines the work procedure.

## Required Skills and Tools

- Invoke `refactoring-playbook` before changing the retry interpreter.
- Invoke `codebase-design` when adding or changing the request Effect seam.
- Use mise for Node/pnpm commands.
- Use Vitest and Effect `TestClock` for deterministic timing.
- Attempt `entire graph search` once when required by repository guidance; if
  unavailable as documented, continue with focused source reads/search.

## Work Procedure

1. Read `mission.md`, `architecture.md`, `validation-contract.md`, `AGENTS.md`,
   `services.yaml`, `library/effect-v4.md`, and the assigned feature.
2. Inspect repository `AGENTS.md`, relevant CONTRIBUTING/test-lane guidance,
   current branch status, and only the focused client/Worker symbols needed.
3. Identify the smallest behavior-preserving seam for the assigned feature.
   Preserve public Promise and `HevyHttpError` contracts and all package
   boundaries.
4. Write focused failing tests first. Tests must exercise public behavior or
   the internal production request Effect seam, never a parallel test-only
   retry implementation.
5. Run the focused test and record the expected red failure.
6. Implement the smallest complete Effect v4 change:
   - typed internal error channels with sufficient metadata;
   - request-local schedule state;
   - Effect Clock/sleep for default timing;
   - custom Promise sleep adaptation;
   - exactly-once resource finalizers;
   - one outer runtime boundary.
7. Run focused tests until green. Add concurrency and late-settlement checks
   where the feature touches shared state, cancellation, observers, or
   resources.
8. Run `mise exec -- pnpm run test:unit` and
   `mise exec -- pnpm run check:types`.
9. If runtime/bundle paths changed, run `test:worker`, `test:worker-http`, and
   `worker:dry-run`.
10. Run formatting/lint checks for changed files. Review the complete diff for
    generated files, Node built-ins, broad types/casts, duplicated policy,
    secrets, and unrelated changes.
11. Add/update the required non-empty Changeset before committing. Use a
    Conventional Commit and include the required Factory co-author. Do not
    push.
12. Return a thorough handoff with exact commands, test identifiers, commit,
    remaining work, and discovered issues.

## Example Handoff

## When to Return to Orchestrator

- Preserving a current behavior conflicts with the approved explicit-deadline
  correction or architecture.
- An Effect v4 API differs from `library/effect-v4.md` in a way that changes the
  design.
- A fix requires public API, package topology, generated output, Node policy, or
  live-service changes.
- Deterministic cancellation/deadline arbitration cannot be expressed without
  adding a new test seam that needs architectural approval.
- Existing unrelated failures prevent verifying the assigned behavior.

# Mission Worker Guidance

## Mission Boundaries (NEVER VIOLATE)

**Repository:** `/root/hevy-mcp-effect-retry-interpreter`

**Branch:** `feat/effect-retry-interpreter`, stacked from PR #1104 commit
`1073abb`. Do not rebase onto main during the mission.

**Ports and services:** No long-running service or claimed port is required.
Do not start persistent watch, dev-server, or browser processes.

**External services:** Deterministic mocked validation only. Do not call the
live Hevy API and do not require, read, print, or persist `HEVY_API_KEY`.

**Off-limits:**

- `packages/hevy-client/src/generated/` must not be edited.
- `/root/hevy-mcp` untracked `.pi-subagents/` and `.worktrees/` are user state.
- PR #1104 and remote branches must not be modified or pushed.
- Do not change public Node compatibility, package topology, or unrelated
  adapters.

If the feature cannot be completed inside these boundaries, return to the
orchestrator.

## Mission Directives

**Tools:** Use mise for all Node/pnpm commands. Use named repository test lanes.
Attempt the documented `entire graph` search first for locate/change work, but
the CLI is known unavailable; after one failed probe, use focused repository
search and reads rather than retrying.

**Skills:** Invoke and follow `refactoring-playbook` for behavior-preserving
migration and `codebase-design` when defining or changing the interpreter
seam. Always follow `mission-worker-base` startup/cleanup.

**Dependencies:** Use the existing `effect@4.0.0-rc.112`. Do not add or
substitute an Effect version or retry library.

**Other requirements:**

- Strict red-green-refactor TDD.
- Preserve Promise-facing APIs and `HevyHttpError` projections.
- Keep exactly one outer Effect runtime boundary per logical request.
- Create schedule state per request, never per client.
- Default backoff uses Effect Clock/sleep; custom Promise sleep remains
  compatible.
- Preserve existing endpoint, safety, commit-state, retry, and diagnostics
  policies instead of creating parallel policy logic.
- No `any`, broad `unknown` helper contracts, manual casts, or Node built-ins in
  runtime-neutral packages.
- Observer callbacks are best-effort and may not duplicate dispatch or
  completion.
- Every opened attempt, signal, body, timer, fiber, and wait scope must finalize
  exactly once.
- Keep hooks enabled and use Conventional Commits with the Factory co-author.
- Before each commit, add the required non-empty Changeset when the diff
  triggers release coverage.

## Coding and Architecture Conventions

- Keep the Kubb client Promise signature unchanged.
- Internal tagged failures must carry all metadata required for exact public
  projection; do not replace `HevyHttpError` with a lossy Effect error class.
- Prefer one deep request-interpreter module/seam over scattered Effect
  wrappers.
- Keep retry eligibility pure. The schedule owns retry index and delay only.
- Use Effect finalizers rather than parallel manual cleanup paths.
- A caller-supplied explicit deadline is authoritative and terminal.
- The immediate implicit read deadline retry does not sleep, open a wait, or
  consume scheduled backoff.

## Testing & Validation Guidance

Workers run the narrowest tests first, then:

- `mise exec -- pnpm run test:unit`
- `mise exec -- pnpm run check:types`
- Runtime compatibility changes also run `test:worker`, `test:worker-http`, and
  `worker:dry-run`.

The milestone validator runs commands from `services.yaml` sequentially.
Maximum concurrent validators is 1 due to current CPU saturation.

Expected stderr from negative-path Worker tests is not a failure when the
command exits zero. Live credential-gated lanes are out of scope.

# Effect v4 Retry Patterns

Worker-facing Effect v4 RC API constraints and approved patterns.

---

- Import `TestClock` from `effect/testing`.
- `Effect.async` does not exist in this version; the callback primitive is
  `Effect.callback`.
- `Effect.tryPromise` accepts an interruption signal and must use an explicit
  catch mapping.
- Use `Schedule.toStep` for the interpreter because it must inspect/cap delay,
  control wait observations, support custom sleep, and classify sleep failure.
- `Schedule.toStepWithSleep` is unsuitable for this lifecycle because it hides
  the sleep seam.
- Schedule steps are stateful. Construct one inside every logical request.
- Schedule completion uses `Pull`/`Cause.Done`; avoid stepping beyond the known
  retry budget or handle completion explicitly.
- Use `Clock.currentTimeMillis` and `Effect.sleep` for default backoff.
- Use `Effect.ensuring` or scoped finalization for cleanup on success, typed
  failure, defect, and interruption.
- Do not pass the caller AbortSignal directly to `Effect.runPromise` unless
  Cause-level interruption is projected back to the established public
  `HevyHttpError`.
- Build one request Effect and call `Effect.runPromise` once at the Promise
  adapter boundary. Do not nest runtime executions.

# User Testing

Validation surfaces, prerequisites, and concurrency guidance.

## Validation Surface

The user-visible surface is the native Promise Hevy client API and its Worker
adapter projection. Use deterministic Vitest client calls, mocked HTTP, local
Wrangler/Workerd integration, package/boundary checks, and build artifacts.
Browser and TUI tools do not apply.

## Validation Prerequisites

- Pinned mise/Node/pnpm toolchain verified.
- Effect v4, Vitest, Nx, Wrangler, and Workerd imports/commands verified.
- Focused tests, unit, Worker, Worker HTTP, Worker dry-run, and type checks
  passed with `HEVY_API_KEY` explicitly unset.
- No allowlist, external account, port, seed data, or live credential is needed.
- TestClock controls Effect time only; actual client tests must execute the
  internal production request Effect under the TestClock layer.

## Validation Concurrency

Maximum concurrent validators: **1**.

Readiness measurements: 8 CPU cores, approximately 13 GiB available memory,
and load average above the core count. Memory could support more, but
Vitest/Nx/Workerd fan out internally and parallel validators would oversubscribe
CPU. Run validation commands sequentially.

## Evidence

Collect terminal command/exit status, exact passing test identifiers, attempt
and callback event arrays, public error field snapshots, TestClock boundaries,
Worker HTTP envelopes, and bundle/boundary/check output as required by
`validation-contract.md`.

# Complete Effect Retry Interpreter

## Plan Overview

Complete the Hevy client retry migration begun in PR #1104 by moving the entire retry execution lifecycle into one Effect v4 program per logical request. The work will land on `feat/effect-retry-interpreter`, stacked from commit `1073abb` at the head of #1104.

The migration must preserve the current Promise-facing public API and runtime behavior while eliminating shared schedule state, making default backoff and resource cleanup Effect-native, and correcting the caller-deadline retry-wait lifecycle defect approved during planning.

## Expected Functionality

### Milestone: Effect Retry Interpreter

1. **Characterize independent retry state and lifecycle behavior**
   - Add regression coverage proving sequential and concurrent operations on one client have independent retry budgets, schedule attempt indexes, cancellation, and observations.
   - Cover retry-wait finalization, cancellation/deadline races, and exact attempt/completion counts.

2. **Build Effect-native attempt and backoff primitives**
   - Represent attempt failures and retry transitions with internal typed errors/unions.
   - Bridge fetch, response consumption, and optional custom sleep through Effect v4 primitives.
   - Use `Effect.ensuring` for attempt listeners, retry-wait scopes, and execution-signal cleanup.
   - Use Effect `Clock`/`Effect.sleep` for default backoff so the actual client path is controllable with `TestClock`.

3. **Integrate the per-request retry interpreter**
   - Replace the imperative retry loop and nested runtime crossings with one recursive Effect program and one `Effect.runPromise` boundary.
   - Instantiate `Schedule.toStep(createRetrySchedule(...))` separately for every logical request.
   - Preserve retry limits, exponential backoff/jitter, `Retry-After`, absolute and per-attempt deadlines, the single fresh-budget read deadline retry, method safety, commit-state metadata, observations, diagnostics, and exhaustion behavior.
   - Correct the explicit caller-deadline path so it does not open/log an impossible retry or leak an unfinished retry-wait scope.
   - Verify Node and Cloudflare Worker compatibility and review affected README guidance for accuracy.

## Architecture

The Kubb client remains the Promise-based adapter boundary. Inside each request, a single Effect program owns the request lifecycle:

1. Acquire the combined caller/deadline execution signal.
2. Create a request-local retry schedule step.
3. Execute one typed attempt Effect.
4. Classify failure through the existing pure safety and endpoint policies.
5. Return terminal errors immediately, refresh the deadline for the one special read retry, or advance the schedule and execute an interruptible backoff Effect.
6. Recurse with updated retry state.
7. Finalize signals, listeners, and observation scopes on success, failure, defect, or interruption.
8. Convert the final Effect to the existing Promise contract exactly once.

The schedule owns timing and retry index only. Existing client policy remains authoritative for whether retrying is safe. Public `HevyHttpError` remains the externally observable error contract; internal Effect failures must never leak as Effect causes.

Package direction remains `hevy-client -> operations -> core -> adapters`. No Node built-ins enter runtime-neutral packages, and generated client files remain untouched.

## Environment Setup

- Worktree: `/root/hevy-mcp-effect-retry-interpreter`
- Branch: `feat/effect-retry-interpreter`
- Stack base: PR #1104 head, commit `1073abb`

### Navigation\
\
[Permalink: Navigation](https://github.com/github/gh-stack#navigation)\
\
Move between branches in the current stack without having to remember branch names.\
\
```\
gh stack up [n]      # Move up n branches (default 1)\
gh stack down [n]    # Move down n branches (default 1)\
gh stack top         # Jump to the top of the stack\
gh stack bottom      # Jump to the bottom of the stack\
gh stack trunk       # Jump to the trunk branch\
gh stack switch      # Interactively pick a branch to switch to\
```\
\
Navigation commands clamp to the bounds of the stack — moving up from the top or down from the bottom is a no-op with a message. If you're on the trunk branch, `up` moves to the first stack branch.\
\
**Examples:**\
\
```\
gh stack up          # move up one layer\
gh stack up 3        # move up three layers\
gh stack down\
gh stack top\
gh stack bottom\
gh stack trunk       # jump to the trunk branch (e.g., main)\
gh stack switch      # shows an interactive picker\
```\
\
### `gh stack feedback`\
\
[Permalink: gh stack feedback](https://github.com/github/gh-stack#gh-stack-feedback)\
\
Share feedback about gh-stack.\
\
```\
gh stack feedback [title]\
```\
\
Opens a GitHub Discussion in the [gh-stack repository](https://github.com/github/gh-stack) to submit feedback. Optionally provide a title for the discussion post.\
\
**Examples:**\
\
```\
gh stack feedback\
gh stack feedback "Support for reordering branches"\
```\
\
### `gh stack alias`\
\
[Permalink: gh stack alias](https://github.com/github/gh-stack#gh-stack-alias)\
\
Create a short command alias so you can type less.\
\
```\
gh stack alias [flags] [name]\
```\
\
Installs a small wrapper script into `~/.local/bin/` that forwards all arguments to `gh stack`. The default alias name is `gs`, but you can choose any name by passing it as an argument. After setup, you can run `gs push` instead of `gh stack push`.\
\
On Windows, automatic alias creation is not supported — the command prints manual instructions for creating a batch file or PowerShell function.\
\
| Flag | Description |\
| --- | --- |\
| `--remove` | Remove a previously created alias |\
\
**Examples:**\
\
```\
# Create the default alias (gs)\
gh stack alias\
#    → now "gs push", "gs view", etc. all work\
\
# Create a custom alias\
gh stack alias gst\
\
# Remove an alias\
gh stack alias --remove\
gh stack alias gst --remove\
```\

## Typical workflow\
\
[Permalink: Typical workflow](https://github.com/github/gh-stack#typical-workflow)\
\
```\
# 1. Start a stack (creates and checks out the first branch)\
gh stack init\
\
# 2. Work on the first layer\
#    ... write code, make commits ...\
\
# 3. Add the next layer\
gh stack add api-routes\
#    ... write code, make commits ...\
\
# 4. Push everything and create Stacked PRs\
gh stack submit\
\
# 5. Reviewer requests changes on the first PR\
gh stack bottom\
#    ... make changes, commit ...\
\
# 6. Rebase the rest of the stack on top of your fix\
gh stack rebase\
\
# 7. Push the updated branches\
gh stack push\
\
# 8. When the first PR is merged, sync the stack\
gh stack sync\
# → prompts to prune merged branches (or use --prune to prune automatically and avoid the prompt)\
```\
\
## Abbreviated workflow\
\
[Permalink: Abbreviated workflow](https://github.com/github/gh-stack#abbreviated-workflow)\
\
If you want to minimize keystrokes, use the `-Am` flags to fold staging, committing, and branch creation into a single command. When you don't pass a branch name, one is auto-generated from the commit message in date+slug format (e.g., `03-24-auth_middleware`).\
\
When a branch has no commits yet (e.g., right after `init`), `add -Am` stages and commits directly on that branch instead of creating a new one. Once a branch has commits, `add -Am` creates a new branch, checks it out, and commits there.\
\
```\
# 1. Start a stack\
gh stack init auth\
#    → creates auth and checks it out\
\
# 2. Write code for the first layer\
#    ... write code ...\
\
# 3. Stage and commit on the current branch\
gh stack add -Am "Auth middleware"\
#    → auth has no commits yet, so the commit lands here\
#      (no new branch is created)\
\
# 4. Write code for the next layer\
#    ... write code ...\
\
# 5. Create the next branch and commit\
gh stack add -Am "API routes"\
#    → auth already has commits, so a new branch is created from the\
#      commit message, checked out, and the commit lands there\
\
# 6. Keep going\
#    ... write code ...\
\
gh stack add -Am "Frontend components"\
#    → creates another branch and commits there\
\
# 7. Push everything and create PRs\
gh stack submit\
```\
\
Compared to the typical workflow, there's no need to name branches, run `git add`, or run `git commit` separately. Each `gh stack add -Am "..."` does it all. Pass an explicit branch name any time you want to control it: `gh stack add -Am "API routes" api-routes`.\
\
## Terminal theme\
\
[Permalink: Terminal theme](https://github.com/github/gh-stack#terminal-theme)\
\
The interactive screens (`submit`, `modify`, and `view`) and all colored command output (status messages, prompts) automatically adapt their colors to your terminal's background, so they're readable on both dark and light themes. The background is detected from the terminal; if a terminal doesn't report it (some SSH or `tmux` setups), the dark palette is used.\
\
Set `GH_STACK_THEME` to force a palette if detection is wrong:\
\
| Value | Behavior |\
| --- | --- |\
| `auto` (default) | Detect from the terminal background |\
| `light` | Force the light palette |\
| `dark` | Force the dark palette |\
\
```\
# Force the light palette\
export GH_STACK_THEME=light && gh stack view\
```\

| --- | --- |\
| 0 | Success |\
| 1 | Generic error |\
| 2 | Not in a stack / stack not found |\
| 3 | Rebase conflict |\
| 4 | GitHub API failure |\
| 5 | Invalid arguments or flags |\
| 6 | Disambiguation required (branch belongs to multiple stacks) |\
| 7 | Rebase already in progress |\
| 8 | Stack is locked by another process |\

# Stacked pull requests CLI commands

Find every command, flag, and exit code for the `gh stack` extension in GitHub CLI.

Copy as Markdown

## In this article

Note

This feature is in public preview and subject to change.

The `gh stack` extension for GitHub CLI creates and manages stacks of pull requests from your local repository. For an introduction to stacks, see [Stacked pull requests](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/reference/stacked-pull-requests).

## [Installation](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/reference/stacked-prs-cli-commands\#installation)

```shell
gh extension install github/gh-stack
```

The extension requires GitHub CLI (`gh`) version 2.0 or later.

Note

The `gh stack` extension uses your GitHub CLI authentication. If you have not authenticated yet, run `gh auth login`.

## [Command summary](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/reference/stacked-prs-cli-commands\#command-summary)

| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`gh stack init`](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/reference/stacked-prs-cli-commands#gh-stack-init) | Initialize a new stack in the current repository. |
| [`gh stack add`](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/reference/stacked-prs-cli-commands#gh-stack-add) | Add a new branch on top of the current stack. |
| [`gh stack view`](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/reference/stacked-prs-cli-commands#gh-stack-view) | View the current stack. |
| [`gh stack checkout`](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/reference/stacked-prs-cli-commands#gh-stack-checkout) | Check out a stack by stack number, pull request number, pull request URL, or branch name. |
| [`gh stack modify`](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/reference/stacked-prs-cli-commands#gh-stack-modify) | Interactively restructure the current stack. |
